title: Emperor Leopold I to Charles II of Spain, autograph cipher letter, Prague 14 Apr 1680 (BNE RES/261/58)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the leaf, in the margin or on the BNE card; none found in print or online (Tomokiyo habsburg.htm, Lasry, three web searches, DECODE ledgers; see NOTES.md).

transcription.source: BNE Digital viewer page 5, single-page PDF (one embedded image 1654 x 2473 px), CC BY 4.0
transcription.notes: Measured distinct 86 counts 4 doubtful readings (181?, 75?, 45?, 104?, 120?) as separate tokens; the plain value count is 85. The long pen-stroke running through most groups is not transcribed; whether it carries meaning is open.

system.summary: Numeric cipher of 250 groups between a clear Spanish opening and closing; 85 distinct values from 10 to 224, none in the 20s, one bigram (62 39) six times; letter, syllable or nomenclator structure not established.
system.sibling_key: none held; Reichskanzlei numeric ciphers (Grana 1664 and 1668, Auer) and the Spanish court's general cipher of the 1680s are untested candidates
system.notes: Values cluster in blocks 10-17, 30-67, 72-105, 108-154 with outliers 181, 202 and 224 (224 four times); the highest value is 224. Leopold writes 1 as 'i' in the hundreds (i23 = 123). Index of coincidence 0.0165; 35 values occur once.

conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau pasted the project's task brief for catalogue no. 1599; no target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: Claude in Chrome for the BNE Digital viewer

solution.what: BNE Digital viewer opened in Chrome without a Cloudflare challenge; page 5 (the letter) fetched as a single-page PDF with the page's own session and its 1654 x 2473 px image extracted.
20 lines, 250 number groups read from the image into transcription.txt; five readings marked doubtful.
Frequencies, value blocks, bigrams: 85 values over 250 groups, IoC 0.0165, 62 39 six times (62 followed by 39 in six of nine occurrences), 59 129 104 twice; value ranges in four blocks with gaps.

Web searches in English and German (Leopold I cipher, Spanish court, Auer, Habsburg ciphers) and the vetting pass of the same day (DECODE ledgers, Tomokiyo habsburg.htm): no decipherment, no key for the Leopold-Charles II correspondence. Leads left: Auer's chapter on imperial ciphers, the Spain chapter in the same volume, OeStA and AHN holdings.

Letter-level homophonic annealer (85 symbols to 24 letters, order-5 Spanish model without spaces, 300,000 steps x 6 restarts) run on two Spanish texts of 250 letters enciphered with random 81-82-symbol homophonic keys.

Same annealer on the real letter, 6 restarts: best score -488.6 gives pseudo-Spanish; the controls reach only 4-22% letter accuracy and score far below their true plaintext (about -380), so the real output is not evidence of a reading.

outcome.method_basis: Ciphertext-only letter-level homophonic annealing could not recover a key on two controls of the same size (4-22% letters correct, search score far below the true plaintext), so its output on the real letter was not accepted; no key or decipherment was found in the literature, the repository or online.
outcome.notes: Next: Auer's chapter on imperial ciphers and the Spain chapter (Navarro Bonilla, Hernandez-Castro) in the same volume; OeStA Spanien and AHN Estado for a Leopold-Charles II key; sibling letter RES/261/73 (catalogue 1600); a syllabic or nomenclator reading of the value blocks.
